neighbours.label: a noun naming a degree or intensity (strength, level, magnitude, amplitude; also rain or light as something that can stop or fade) as the subject whose extent is about to be stated
fire: Engineers measured how the intensity of the beam changes with distance.
Their military strength was never great enough to threaten the capital.
By evening the wind had dropped and the boats went out.
Nobody yet knows the magnitude of the losses caused by the flood.
The water level in the reservoir was lower than last year.
The plot shows how the amplitude of the wave decays over time.
Her influence over the committee was limited from the start.
Once the snow had eased, the plows cleared the road.
quiet: Engineers measured the beam with a ruler and wrote down the result.
Their military museum was never large enough to hold the collection.
By evening the guests had arrived and the band began to play.
Nobody yet knows the names of the families moved after the flood.
The fishing club at the reservoir was founded last year.
The plot shows where the birds nest along the river.
Her sister on the committee was a lawyer from Boston.
Once the children had eaten, the teacher read a story.

short: intensity noun whose degree is stated
notes: Card: ' level(s)', ' magnitude', ' amplitude', ' strength', 'the rain had stopped'; the output direction promotes ' level', ' intensity', ' magnitude' on this pole. Probes: strength was 0.65, rain had stopped 0.60, noise level 0.51, magnitude … has 0.46, amplitude 0.28; non-scalar subjects (author of the book, colour of the lamp) 0.01-0.03.
